Frequently asked questions

What does 'trending' mean on explainx.ai?
Trending on explainx.ai means a page — whether an AI skill, MCP server, tool, agent, LLM, loop, slash command, or blog post — has earned a high score among real users in a given time window (today, last 7 days, or last 30 days). All content types are ranked together in a single list by score, so the highest-scoring item always appears at the top regardless of type.
How often does the trending page update?
The trending page is served with a 30-minute ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) cache. Scores are updated in real time whenever a user visits any content page on explainx.ai, but the ranked list refreshes approximately every 30 minutes.
What types of content appear in the trending list?
explainx.ai tracks activity across 14 content types: blog posts, AI skills, AI tools, MCP servers, AI agents, LLMs (large language models), tech devices, agent loops, slash commands, prompt collections, plugins, workshops, bootcamps, and video courses. All types are merged into a single ranked feed so you can see the highest-scoring content across the entire platform at a glance.
How can I find trending MCP servers?
MCP servers appear inline in the unified trending list with an 'mcp' badge. You can also filter by time period (Today, 7 days, 30 days) using the tabs at the top to discover which MCP servers the community is exploring right now.
What is a trending score?
Each item earns a score that combines three signals: real page visits from the explainx.ai community, broader internet search interest in that topic, and how directly the content impacts AI practitioners — whether it's a skill they can install today, a workshop they can attend, or a tool that changes how they work. Content with strong real-world AI impact scores higher than passive reads alone.
